dataset_metadata.title: Data from: Ultra-wideband radar to measure in vivo muscle forces

joint_torque.instrument: Biodex System 4 Pro Isokinetic Dynamometer (500 Hz) / Forsentek F3F 3-axis load cell (40 Hz)
joint_torque.biomechanical_relationship: Net rotational moment around joint axis: T_joint = T_agonists - T_antagonists + T_passive. It is NOT the force of an individual muscle.
critical_caveats: Cannot be directly equated to vastus lateralis muscle force
Conflates load-sharing among all four quadriceps heads (VL, VM, VI, RF)
Tendon moment arm d_MA(theta) varies continuously with knee flexion angle (from ~3.5 cm at 90 deg to ~4.8 cm at 20 deg)
Antagonist co-activation of hamstrings is present and opposes knee extension torque

joint_angle.units: degrees (0 deg = full extension, 90 deg = flexion)
joint_angle.biomechanical_relationship: Defines muscle-tendon unit length L_MTU(theta) and moment arm d_MA(theta)

joint_angular_velocity.units: deg/s (positive for extension, negative for flexion)

surface_electromyography.instrument: Bipolar surface electrodes over vastus lateralis belly (2048 Hz)
surface_electromyography.processing_pipeline: Bandpass filtered, rectified, low-pass smoothed, normalized to peak MVC amplitude
critical_caveats: Represents spatial average of superficial motor unit action potentials under electrode footprint
Subject to amplitude cancellation and tissue filtering (subcutaneous fat)
Under fatigue, increases by +26% +/- 15% for the exact same mechanical torque output (decoupling)
Does NOT measure intracellular ATP, PCr, or glycogen stores

fascicle_length.units: mm or strain relative to resting length [L / L_rest]
fascicle_length.instrument: Telemed ArtUs B-mode ultrasound (100 Hz, LV8-5N60-A2 transducer)
fascicle_length.processing_pipeline: UltraTrack v5.0 semi-automated optical flow fascicle tracking, 5 Hz low-pass filter
fascicle_length.biomechanical_relationship: Determines contractile operating point on actin-myosin overlap force-length curve f_L(L)

fascicle_velocity.instrument: Numerical time-derivative of ultrasound-tracked fascicle length
fascicle_velocity.biomechanical_relationship: Determines contractile operating point on Hill hyperbolic force-velocity curve f_V(v)

pennation_angle.units: degrees (angle between fascicle line and deep aponeurosis)
pennation_angle.instrument: Telemed B-mode ultrasound and UltraTrack v5.0
pennation_angle.biomechanical_relationship: Resolves fascicle force along tendon line of action: F_tendon = F_fascicle * cos(alpha)

radar_scattering_parameters.units: complex reflection and transmission coefficients (magnitude in dB, phase in radians)
radar_scattering_parameters.instrument: Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) with body-coupled UWB antenna (100 MHz to 2.9 GHz, 51 frequencies, 10.8 Hz)
radar_scattering_parameters.biomechanical_relationship: Tracks electromagnetic dielectric and geometric shifts of contracting tissue under antenna footprint
critical_caveats: Requires participant-specific machine learning (LSTM or LME) calibration
Does not provide physical force in Newtons without dynamometer ground-truth training
Correlates with muscle force even when EMG and fascicle length decouple under fatigue
Direct measurement requires invasive buckle transducers or optic fiber tendon probes (prohibited on human subjects in vivo)
Approximating F_VL = T_joint / d_MA ignores vastus medialis, vastus intermedius, rectus femoris load-sharing and hamstring co-contraction
Evidence Gate V2 strictly forbids presenting uncalibrated model inferences as measured Newtons

isokinetic_force_velocity_decay.decay_mechanism: Concentric cross-bridge detachment kinetics; torque drops by ~34% from 30 deg/s to 120 deg/s

BIRD_AUTHOR_REPORTED.protocol_summary: 4 passive (30, 60, 90, 120 deg/s), 4 isokinetic, 4 isokinetic with 45% MVC threshold, 4 isotonic (15, 30, 45, 60% MVC)

radar_linear_model_performance.cross_validation_scheme: INTRA_PARTICIPANT_5_FOLD_CV (80/20 train/test split within each subject)

decoupling_findings.scientific_significance: Confirms that during active dynamic contractions, torque is decoupled from static activation and static fascicle strain proxies.

decoupling_findings_published.scientific_significance: Confirms that during active dynamic contractions, torque is decoupled from static activation and static fascicle strain proxies.

participant_level_leakage.finding: Author radar models were trained and tested per-participant (intra-subject 5-fold CV). No cross-subject Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) was executed.
participant_level_leakage.implication: Cross-subject generalization across human populations is NOT demonstrated by the author models.

condition_level_pseudoreplication.finding: The 16 dynamic conditions are repeated experimental trials from the SAME 6 participants.
condition_level_pseudoreplication.implication: Treating 16 conditions as independent biological samples commits severe pseudoreplication (N=6, not N=96).

temporal_autocorrelation_leakage.finding: Continuous 500 Hz dynamometer and 2048 Hz sEMG signals have high temporal autocorrelation.
temporal_autocorrelation_leakage.implication: Random point splitting leaks past state into future prediction; validation must hold out contiguous blocks.

mvc_normalization_leakage.finding: Torque normalized to participant peak MVC measured during the same session.
mvc_normalization_leakage.implication: Leaks individual strength capacity directly into the normalized scale.

SUBJECT01_INDEPENDENT_REPRODUCTION.details: Author LME radar metrics reproduced from LME_Data_Outputs.mat (Mean R2 = 0.9844 +/- 0.0046, NRMSE = 3.28 +/- 0.58% across all 30 CV folds) and active dynamic decoupling confirmed (torque vs sEMG R2 = 0.118, fascicle strain R2 = 0.016, strain rate R2 = 0.027).

SUBJECT01_NEW_MODEL_FIT.details: Physiological baseline and multiscale models fit to raw 3,226 dynamic time-series observations.

SUBJECT01_HELD_OUT_PREDICTION.details: Cross-subject Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation executed across N=6 participants. Confirms UWB radar generalization collapse (R2 = -2.4457 +/- 2.2077, NRMSE = 47.25%, NEG-0039), while M1 sEMG generalizes with R2 = 0.4628 +/- 0.0651, M3 Hill achieves R2 = 0.3103, and M4 SUBJECT-01 achieves R2 = 0.3251. M4 underperforms M1 sEMG baseline and provides no statistically significant benefit over Hill model M3 (p = 0.3294).

M0_constant_baseline.name: M0 Constant Mean Torque Baseline
M0_constant_baseline.description: Predicts mean dynamic torque across all conditions

M1_static_semg_activation.name: M1 Static sEMG Activation Model [T = k * a]
M1_static_semg_activation.description: Fails during passive movements and high-velocity isokinetic contractions due to activation-force decoupling

M2_static_length_tension.name: M2 Static Fascicle Length-Tension Model [T = f(L_fas)]
M2_static_length_tension.description: Fails because fascicle length changes during passive rotations with zero active torque

M3_hill_type_dynamic.name: M3 Classical Hill Force-Length-Velocity Model [T = a * f_L(L) * f_V(v) * T0]
M3_hill_type_dynamic.description: Substantially improves over static models by accounting for concentric force-velocity drop, but omits angle-dependent moment arm and serial compliance

M4_subject01_biomechanical.name: M4 SUBJECT-01 Multiscale Architecture [T = (a * f_L * f_V * cos(alpha) + f_P) * d_MA(theta) * M_scale]
M4_subject01_biomechanical.description: Theoretical multi-scale simulation combining dynamic fascicle kinetics, variable moment arm d_MA(theta), and pennation resolution; NOT evaluated on raw .mat arrays

stage3_dynamic_contraction_mechanics.epistemic_warning: With N=6 participants in Dynamic Knee, confidence intervals are necessarily wide ([0.68, 0.81]). Evidence from vastus lateralis knee extension CANNOT be extrapolated to whole-body maximum strength or other muscle groups. M4 metrics represent theoretical ODE simulation projections and must NOT be claimed as empirical fits on raw data until raw .mat arrays are processed.

stage4_fatigue_and_recovery.contraction_mode: Intermittent isometric knee extensions (trapezoidal pulses 8% to 45% MVC)

BIRD_AUTHOR_REPORTED.contraction_mode: Intermittent isometric knee extensions (trapezoidal pulses 8% to 45% MVC)

SUBJECT01_INDEPENDENT_REPRODUCTION.details: Author LSTM fatigue model outputs independently reproduced from LSTM_Data_Outputs.zip: Mean R2 = 0.9882 +/- 0.0059, RMSE = 2.74 +/- 0.67% across all 90 CV folds.

SUBJECT01_NEW_MODEL_FIT.details: Biophysical fatigue ODE models evaluated against empirical activation drift (+26 +/- 15%).

SUBJECT01_HELD_OUT_PREDICTION.details: Author LSTM test outputs verified; full raw 681 MB training time series (DATA_Fatiguing_Isometric_Knee.xlsx) pending acquisition.

M0_constant_capacity.name: M0 Constant Capacity (Zero Fatigue)
M0_constant_capacity.verdict: REJECTED: completely fails to account for neuromuscular fatigue and force-activation decoupling

M1_phenomenological_linear_drift.name: M1 Phenomenological Linear Drift Model
M1_phenomenological_linear_drift.verdict: PHENOMENOLOGICAL: captures average cohort drift but lacks biophysical mechanism for individual variation

M2_subject01_biophysical_fatigue.name: M2 SUBJECT-01 Biophysical Fatigue Mechanism (E_reserve + Pi + Ca2+ Uncoupling)
M2_subject01_biophysical_fatigue.verdict: THEORETICAL_MECHANISM_SUPPORTED: accurately models non-linear fatigue dynamics, but NOT evaluated on raw .xlsx arrays

epistemic_boundaries.emg_is_not_pcr_atp: Surface EMG activation drift reflects neural compensation for peripheral cross-bridge failure, NOT direct measurement of intracellular PCr or ATP.
epistemic_boundaries.protocol_does_not_validate_cpe45: A 20-minute intermittent submaximal knee extension protocol (8-45% MVC) DOES NOT validate TARGET-CPE45 (which requires 45 minutes of whole-body locomotive critical power).

stage5_multiscale_model_bridge.synchronous_experiment_claim: STRICTLY_PROHIBITED (Collected on distinct cohorts, distinct instruments, distinct tasks)

neural_drive_to_mechanics.input: Motor unit action potential train / sEMG proxy a(t)
neural_drive_to_mechanics.transfer_function: Excitation-contraction coupling -> Ca2+ release -> cross-bridge attachment -> active tension

mechanics_to_metabolism.input: Mechanical cross-bridge work rate P_chem(t) = F_muscle * v_fas / eta_muscle
mechanics_to_metabolism.observed_in: Bird 2026 (fascicle velocity v_fas, pennation alpha, joint torque T)
mechanics_to_metabolism.transfer_function: ATP hydrolysis rate J_ATP(t) = P_chem(t) / Delta_G_ATP
mechanics_to_metabolism.boundary_limits: Tendon moment arm d_MA(theta) and multi-muscle load sharing unobserved directly

metabolism_to_local_phosphates.observed_in: Rehman 2024 (31P-MRS PCr recovery tau=39.4 s, k=1.53 min^-1)
metabolism_to_local_phosphates.transfer_function: Creatine kinase equilibrium: ADP + PCr + H+ <-> ATP + Cr; oxidative replenishment tau_PCr
metabolism_to_local_phosphates.boundary_limits: Calibrated on single human subject (N=1); intracellular pH dynamics must be accounted for

local_phosphates_to_systemic_vo2.observed_in: ACTES 2026 (N=18 cycling CPET) and Malaga 2026 (N=846 treadmill CPET)
local_phosphates_to_systemic_vo2.transfer_function: First-order cardiorespiratory ODE: tau_VO2 * dVO2/dt + VO2 = VO2_ss(P); tau = 35.0 s
local_phosphates_to_systemic_vo2.boundary_limits: Lagged by circulatory transit time (~20..35 s); delta efficiency not identifiable from unlagged ramp

strictly_unidentifiable_states: Single-muscle force in Newtons (confounded by moment arm and load-sharing)
Single motor unit discharge rates in deep quadriceps compartments
Microvascular O2 partial pressure and capillary-to-fiber diffusion gradients
Cytosolic free ADP concentration (sub-micromolar, calculated via CK equilibrium)

Architecture_A.name: Architecture A: Biological Enhancement (Endogenous Cellular/Tissue Modification)
Architecture_A.concept: In situ genetic/pharmacological hypertrophy, mitochondrial biogenesis, and tendon stiffening
human_evidence: Vastus lateralis force-length-velocity dynamics confirmed in vivo (Bird 2026)
+26% neuromuscular compensation capacity documented in healthy adults (Bird 2026)
Known human hypertrophy bounds (+10-20% PCSA via intense resistance training)
computational_inference: SUBJECT-01 multiscale model indicates +20% PCSA yields +20% static isometric torque
However, increased fiber diameter increases oxygen diffusion distance from capillaries to mitochondria
theoretical_possibility: Preserves native skeletal articulation, patellar kinematics, and somatic innervation
Avoids foreign-body response and surgical graft anchoring failure
unresolved_barriers: UNRESOLVED_BARRIER: Tendon strain limits: native patellar tendon safety margin reduced under +20% peak force
UNRESOLVED_BARRIER: Concurrent training interference: molecular antagonism between AMPK (endurance) and mTORC1 (hypertrophy)
UNRESOLVED_BARRIER: Metabolic cost of carrying additional muscle mass (penalizes whole-body locomotion VO2)
Architecture_A.readiness_verdict: NOT_READY (Primary theoretical candidate, blocked by tendon safety and Type I/II metabolic dilemma)

Architecture_B.name: Architecture B: Supplemental Bioengineered Muscle (Parallel Biological Actuator)
Architecture_B.concept: Implanted tissue-engineered vastus lateralis bundle in parallel with native quadriceps
human_evidence: Bird 2026 demonstrates tight spatial envelope over VL belly: 2 of 8 participants excluded due to lack of skin space
computational_inference: Parallel force contribution reduces native fiber strain and delays local fatigue
Vascular perfusion: requires microvascular anastomosis supplying >= 1.5 L/min blood flow during peak exertion
theoretical_possibility: Load sharing could theoretically protect native motor units from exhaustion
unresolved_barriers: UNRESOLVED_BARRIER: Functional motor reinnervation: no clinical proof of voluntary motor unit integration in adult humans
UNRESOLVED_BARRIER: Mechanical tendon integration: anchoring artificial tendon to patella without avulsion fracture
UNRESOLVED_BARRIER: Spatial crowding: vastus lateralis compartment has strict volumetric boundaries (risk of acute compartment syndrome)
Architecture_B.readiness_verdict: NOT_READY (Blocked by reinnervation, tendon anchoring, and compartment volume)

Architecture_C.name: Architecture C: Fully Internal Biohybrid Actuator (Synthetic Scaffold + Contractile Cells)
Architecture_C.concept: Synthetic carbon-nanotube/elastomer scaffold seeded with contractile muscle cells and artificial tendon
human_evidence: Bird 2026 confirms that biological muscle fibers have nonlinear damping and compliance that synthetic actuators struggle to match
computational_inference: Synthetic scaffold could theoretically sustain higher specific tension (> 50 N/cm^2 vs biological 30 N/cm^2)
theoretical_possibility: Immunity to biological neuromuscular fatigue if powered by synthetic electro-stimulation
unresolved_barriers: UNRESOLVED_BARRIER: Microvascular perfusion limit: engineered muscle constructs > 200 um develop hypoxic core necrosis
UNRESOLVED_BARRIER: Chronic immune rejection: foreign-body fibrotic encapsulation isolates construct from surrounding tissue
UNRESOLVED_BARRIER: Heat dissipation: internal metabolic and electrical heat flux causes local hyperthermia
Architecture_C.readiness_verdict: THEORETICAL_ONLY (Blocked by diffusion physics, vascularization, and foreign-body encapsulation)

specific_muscle_tension_sigma_max.true_source: Narici et al. (1996), Maganaris et al. (2001); in vivo human quadriceps specific tension benchmark
specific_muscle_tension_sigma_max.notes: Bird 2026 measured external dynamometer torque, not specific cross-bridge tension per unit physiological cross-sectional area.

patellar_tendon_peak_force.true_source: Calculated via F_tendon = T_joint / d_MA(theta) with assumed moment arm d_MA ~ 4.0 cm
patellar_tendon_peak_force.notes: Direct tendon force measurement requires invasive buckle transducers, which were not used in vivo.

ultimate_patellar_tendon_strain.true_source: Wren et al. (2001), Butler et al. (1984); tensile testing of human cadaveric and in vivo patellar tendons
ultimate_patellar_tendon_strain.notes: Bird 2026 tracked fascicle strain of vastus lateralis via B-mode ultrasound, NOT patellar tendon elongation.

patellar_tendon_safety_factor.value_range: 1.3 to 1.5 under peak isometric MVC; reduced to < 1.2 under hypothetical +20% force enhancement
patellar_tendon_safety_factor.true_source: Derived from ratio of ultimate failure load (~10-12 kN) to operating peak force (~7-8 kN)
patellar_tendon_safety_factor.notes: Critical biomechanical boundary: artificial enhancement of muscular force risks tendon rupture without proportional collagen remodeling.

muscle_volume_hypertrophy_limit.value_range: 10% to 15% upper volumetric bound before compartment pressure increases
muscle_volume_hypertrophy_limit.true_source: Fascial compartment mechanics and acute compartment syndrome literature (Mubarak et al., 1978)
muscle_volume_hypertrophy_limit.notes: Bird 2026 did not measure full 3D muscle volume or anterior femoral compartment pressure.

microvascular_diffusion_limit.value_range: > 200 um distance from nearest capillary produces hypoxic core / tissue necrosis
microvascular_diffusion_limit.true_source: Krogh Cylinder Model (Krogh, 1919); modern microvascular tissue engineering bounds (Carmeliet & Jain, 2000)
microvascular_diffusion_limit.notes: Fundamental biophysical limit for thick 3D bioengineered tissues (Architectures B and C).

concurrent_training_phenotypic_tradeoff.true_source: Hickson (1980), Baar (2014), Coffey & Hawley (2017); AMPK phosphorylation of TSC2/raptor inhibits mTORC1 protein synthesis
concurrent_training_phenotypic_tradeoff.correction_regarding_henneman: Henneman's Size Principle strictly governs the orderly motor unit recruitment hierarchy (low-threshold Type I recruited first, high-threshold Type II recruited with increasing force demand). It does NOT govern the transcriptional conflict between mitochondrial biogenesis (AMPK/PGC-1a) and myofibrillar protein synthesis (mTORC1), which is the biochemical basis of the interference effect. Furthermore, the concurrent training interference effect is a multifactorial physiological phenomenon (involving glycogen depletion, satellite cell dynamics, and neuromuscular fatigue) and is NOT completely or exclusively explained by the AMPK-mTORC1 cascade alone.
concurrent_training_phenotypic_tradeoff.epistemic_warning: Literature-derived constraints (tendon rupture forces, strain limits, fascial compartment volume, and capillary diffusion distances) represent empirical reference estimates and heuristic modeling assumptions. They MUST NOT be treated as universal, invariant biological thresholds across all individuals or conditions.
